$comment: Exact versions of everything vendored into a build. Committed; the
binaries themselves never are - CI builds them from these pins and
uploads them as artefacts. Changing a pin is a pull request with a
reason, and it re-runs the parity check in docs/adr/spikes/loom-native.md.

loom.note: Head of master on 2026-09-07. The published maps were built from an unpinned master build; the spike checks whether that output matches this commit.

loom_windows_port.note: MSYS2/UCRT64 build scripts and compatibility patches for Windows.

engine.note: The same bytes on every machine. At v0.8.3 every text file the engine reads or writes is UTF-8 with LF, the service day is formatted without %-d or the locale's names, and --schema writes its bytes past the console's text layer, so a Windows sidecar can build a map, plan an export and print the schema the fingerprint below was taken from (E19; engine issue 22). Before it, v0.8.2 made map.build's line_order a preference rather than a whitelist (A4-02, engine issue 28). Additive at protocol 1 and the schema is byte-identical, so the tag is the gate. The handshake compares version and protocol with engine.info and refuses any other; the vendoring job installs the package at the tag.

python.note: Upstream publishes no checksum manifest and no per-asset .sha256, so these hashes were computed on first download and are what every later build is checked against. A changed hash means the asset changed, which is the point.
python.licence_check: Verified 2026-09-07: the interpreter links libedit, not GNU readline, and _dbm links only libSystem - no GDBM. Both are GPL components that must stay out; see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. The Windows asset, listed 2026-09-12, has no readline and no _dbm or _gdbm extension; darwin-x64 has the same names as darwin-arm64.

ffmpeg.note: Built in this repository by scripts/vendor-ffmpeg.sh, in the ffmpeg jobs of .github/workflows/vendor.yml, natively on each target (ADR-040, amending ADR-012): ffmpeg and ffprobe only (the engine finds ffprobe beside SCHEMATIC_FFMPEG by name). FFmpeg from its release tarball, x264 from a commit, both checked by sha256 before use; x264 is the only external library, and zlib, which the PNG codecs need, is the operating system's on macOS and Linux and built statically from its release tarball on Windows, which has none. `source.sha256` was computed on download on 2026-09-13 (FFmpeg publishes a GPG signature, not a checksum). `x264.sha256` is of the uncompressed tar `git archive --format=tar --prefix=x264-<commit>/` writes for the commit, which is byte for byte the tar inside VideoLAN GitLab's .tar.bz2 of it; `x264.commit` is master's head since 2025-09-10, and the commit BtbN's builds pin. `zlib.sha256` matches the digest GitHub records for the release asset. Per target: `configure` is FFmpeg's configure line exactly as `ffmpeg -version` prints it; `x264_configure` and `zlib_configure` are the arguments given to each configure besides `--prefix`, which names the build's own dependency folder; `reports` is the token after 'ffmpeg version '. The script refuses to build when the lines it composes differ from these, and the proof refuses a binary whose -version differs.
ffmpeg.licence: GPL-3.0-or-later: every target is configured --enable-gpl --enable-version3 and links x264 (GPL-2.0-or-later); none is --enable-nonfree

source.licence: LGPL-2.1-or-later, GPL-2.0-or-later with --enable-gpl, and the version 3 of each with --enable-version3
